We need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have IR spectrum data: wavenumbers list includes 1606, 1587 etc. No strong carbonyl stretch (~1700 cm-1). The list seems to have only O-H (3357) and many C-H stretches. No carbonyl peak. So likely zero carbonyl groups.

But we should verify maybe other data like NMR could indicate carbonyl carbon shift (~200 ppm). Could retrieve carbon shifts. But IR lacking carbonyl suggests none. However could be conjugated carbonyl with lower intensity? Usually still around 1680-1740. Not present. So answer 0.

We can also retrieve carbon NMR to see if any carbonyl signals. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool.
